title: Whole Numbers up to Billions: Place Value and Rounding
seo_title: Whole Numbers up to Billions – Primary 6 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Count, read and write whole numbers up to billions; give the place value of digits; compare, order and round large numbers. (summary of the NERDC Primary 6 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 maths worksheets on large whole numbers: place value up to billions, reading and writing numbers, comparing and ordering, and rounding. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Each comma group has hundreds, tens and units.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Group the digits in threes from the right: billions, millions, thousands, units. 3,045,720,000 is three billion, forty-five million, seven hundred and twenty thousand.
  • 1 thousand = 1,000; 1 million = 1,000 thousands; 1 billion = 1,000 millions.
  • To round, look at the next digit to the right: 5 or more rounds up.

Examples

Example

Value of 7 in 4,371,256

7 is in the ten thousands place

Answer: 70,000

Example

Round 6,482,900 to the nearest million

Next digit 4

Answer: 6,000,000

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing too few zerosOne billion has nine zeros: 1,000,000,000.
Comparing numbers of different lengths from the leftCount the digits first.
Rounding the wrong placeUnderline the place you round to first.

faq.q: How many millions make a billion?
What is the population of Nigeria in figures?
Why do we round large numbers?
faq.a: To make them easier to read and remember.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 2 is in the hundred thousands place, so it is worth 2 hundred thousands = 200,000. The digit is 2, but its value is 200,000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 1 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 1 thousand = 1,000. The digit is 1, but its value is 1,000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 7 is in the millions place, so it is worth 7 million = 7,000,000. The digit is 7, but its value is 7,000,000.

items.q: In 1,860,537, which digit is in the hundred thousands place?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands, millions. In 1,860,537 the hundred thousands digit is 8, worth 800,000.

items.q: In 2,879,516, which digit is in the ten thousands place?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands, millions. In 2,879,516 the ten thousands digit is 7, worth 70,000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 6 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 6 ten thousands = 60,000. The digit is 6, but its value is 60,000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 4 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 4 hundreds = 400. The digit is 4, but its value is 400.

items.q: Which number has a 5 in the hundred thousands place?
items.e: The hundred thousands place is the 6th digit from the right (the first digit after the millions). In 3,521,986 the 5 is there, so it is worth 500,000.
Put each digit in its place and write 0 in every empty place: 3,000,000 + 400,000 + 7,000 + 20 = 3,407,020.
Put each digit in its place and write 0 in every empty place: 6,000,000 + 50,000 + 300 = 6,050,300.

items.q: Which number is four million, sixty thousand and five?
items.e: Write each part in its group of three digits: four million → 4, sixty thousand → 060, then 005. Fill every empty place with 0: 4,060,005.

items.q: Which number is two million, three hundred and seven thousand and eighty?
items.e: Write each part in its group of three digits: two million → 2, three hundred and seven thousand → 307, then 080. Fill every empty place with 0: 2,307,080.

items.q: Which number is nine million, four thousand, three hundred?
items.e: Write each part in its group of three digits: nine million → 9, four thousand → 004, then 300. Fill every empty place with 0: 9,004,300.

items.q: In 3,606,000, how many times greater is the value of the first 6 than the value of the second 6?
items.e: The first 6 is worth 600,000. The second 6 is worth 6,000. 600,000 ÷ 6,000 = 100. Each place to the left is worth 10 times more, and the 6s are two places apart: 10 × 10 = 100. (594,000 is the difference, not how many times greater.)

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 7 is in the hundred thousands place, so it is worth 7 hundred thousands = 700,000. The digit is 7, but its value is 700,000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 3 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 3 thousands = 3,000. The digit is 3, but its value is 3,000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 8 is in the millions place, so it is worth 8 million = 8,000,000. The digit is 8, but its value is 8,000,000.

items.q: In 4,560,218, which digit is in the hundred thousands place?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands, millions. In 4,560,218 the hundred thousands digit is 5, worth 500,000.

items.q: In 9,532,460, which digit is in the ten thousands place?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands, millions. In 9,532,460 the ten thousands digit is 3, worth 30,000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 7 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 7 ten thousands = 70,000. The digit is 7, but its value is 70,000.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the ten thousands place: 9 ten thousands is more than 8 ten thousands. So 6,098,450 > 6,089,450.

items.q: What is 10,000 more than 4,995,300?
items.e: Add 1 to the ten thousands digit: 9 ten thousands + 1 = 10 ten thousands. Exchange them for 1 hundred thousand, then 9 + 1 = 10 hundred thousands, so exchange again for 1 million. 4,995,300 + 10,000 = 5,005,300.

items.q: What is 100,000 less than 2,034,500?
items.e: There are 0 hundred thousands, so exchange 1 million for 10 hundred thousands. 10 − 1 = 9 hundred thousands and 1 million is left. 2,034,500 − 100,000 = 1,934,500.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the thousands place: 9 thousands is more than 2 thousands. So 3,869,214 > 3,862,194. 3,869,214 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundred thousands place: 6 hundred thousands is more than 4 hundred thousands. So 8,643,571 > 8,467,531. 8,467,531 is the smallest.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 2,000,000 to 3,000,000 there are 10 equal jumps, so each mark is 100,000, not 10,000. The arrow is 7 marks after 2,000,000: 2,000,000 + 700,000 = 2,700,000.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 5,000,000 to 6,000,000 there are 10 equal jumps, so each mark is 100,000, not 10,000. The arrow is 4 marks after 5,000,000: 5,000,000 + 400,000 = 5,400,000.

items.q: Put 9,631,457, 9,635,147, 9,631,745 in order from smallest to greatest.
Put 9,862,753, 9,865,327, 9,268,357 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 9,268,357 < 9,862,753 (hundred thousands: 2 < 8). 9,862,753 < 9,865,327 (thousands: 2 < 5). So the order is 9,268,357, 9,862,753, 9,865,327.

items.q: Put 7,286,395, 7,285,693, 7,286,953 in order from greatest to smallest.
5,2☐8,400 > 5,276,000. Which digit could go in the box?
items.e: The millions and hundred thousands are the same. Compare the ten thousands: the box must be more than 7, or equal to 7. 4, 5 and 6 are too small. 5,288,400 > 5,276,000.

items.q: 3,☐45,000 < 3,412,900. Which digit could go in the box?
items.e: The millions are the same. Compare the hundred thousands: the box must be less than 4. If it is 4, compare the ten thousands: 4 > 1, so 3,445,000 would be too big. 3,345,000 < 3,412,900.

items.q: Use each of the digits 4, 0, 8, 2, 6, 1 and 9 once. What is the greatest 7-digit number you can make?
items.e: Put the biggest digit in the millions place, then the next biggest, and so on: 9, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1, 0. The greatest number is 9,864,210.

items.q: Put 4,792,638, 4,793,268, 4,729,368 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 4,729,368 < 4,792,638 (ten thousands: 2 < 9). 4,792,638 < 4,793,268 (thousands: 2 < 3). So the order is 4,729,368, 4,792,638, 4,793,268.

items.q: Put 4,387,215, 4,873,215, 4,782,315 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 4,387,215 < 4,782,315 (hundred thousands: 3 < 7). 4,782,315 < 4,873,215 (hundred thousands: 7 < 8). So the order is 4,387,215, 4,782,315, 4,873,215.

items.q: Put 5,764,913, 5,746,193, 5,761,493 in order from greatest to smallest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 5,746,193 < 5,761,493 (ten thousands: 4 < 6). 5,761,493 < 5,764,913 (thousands: 1 < 4). So the order is 5,764,913, 5,761,493, 5,746,193.

items.q: Put 8,946,125, 8,946,251, 8,496,521 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 8,496,521 < 8,946,125 (hundred thousands: 4 < 9). 8,946,125 < 8,946,251 (hundreds: 1 < 2). So the order is 8,496,521, 8,946,125, 8,946,251.

items.q: Put 2,853,146, 2,814,536, 2,854,316 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 2,814,536 < 2,853,146 (ten thousands: 1 < 5). 2,853,146 < 2,854,316 (thousands: 3 < 4). So the order is 2,814,536, 2,853,146, 2,854,316.

items.q: Put 8,293,457, 8,932,457, 8,239,754 in order from greatest to smallest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 8,239,754 < 8,293,457 (ten thousands: 3 < 9). 8,293,457 < 8,932,457 (hundred thousands: 2 < 9). So the order is 8,932,457, 8,293,457, 8,239,754.

items.q: Put 8,643,172, 8,641,732, 8,673,412 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 8,641,732 < 8,643,172 (thousands: 1 < 3). 8,643,172 < 8,673,412 (ten thousands: 4 < 7). So the order is 8,641,732, 8,643,172, 8,673,412.

items.q: Round 103,759 to the nearest 1,000.
items.e: 103,759 is between 103,000 and 104,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 7. 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 104,000.

items.q: Round 867,954 to the nearest 10,000.
items.e: 867,954 is between 860,000 and 870,000. Look at the thousands digit: 7. 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 870,000.

items.q: Round 9,600,519 to the nearest 10.
items.e: 9,600,519 is between 9,600,510 and 9,600,520. Look at the units digit: 9. 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 9,600,520.

items.q: Round 532,697 to the nearest 100.
items.e: 532,697 is between 532,600 and 532,700. Look at the tens digit: 9. 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 532,700.

items.q: Round 8,203,002 to the nearest 100,000.
items.e: 8,203,002 is between 8,200,000 and 8,300,000. Look at the ten thousands digit: 0. 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 8,200,000.

items.q: Round 6,433,411 to the nearest 1,000,000.
items.e: 6,433,411 is between 6,000,000 and 7,000,000. Look at the hundred thousands digit: 4. 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 6,000,000.

items.q: Round 2,208,473 to the nearest 1,000.
items.e: 2,208,473 is between 2,208,000 and 2,209,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 4. 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 2,208,000.

items.q: Round 6,687,063 to the nearest 10,000.
items.e: 6,687,063 is between 6,680,000 and 6,690,000. Look at the thousands digit: 7. 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 6,690,000.

items.q: Round 2,450,000 to the nearest 100,000.
items.e: 2,450,000 is exactly halfway between 2,400,000 and 2,500,000. A number that is exactly halfway rounds up. Answer: 2,500,000.

items.q: Round 3,500,000 to the nearest 1,000,000.
items.e: 3,500,000 is exactly halfway between 3,000,000 and 4,000,000. A number that is exactly halfway rounds up. Answer: 4,000,000.

items.q: Round 4,857,762 to the nearest 10,000.
items.e: 4,857,762 is between 4,850,000 and 4,860,000. Look at the thousands digit: 7. 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 4,860,000.

items.q: Round 341,157 to the nearest 100,000.
items.e: 341,157 is between 300,000 and 400,000. Look at the ten thousands digit: 4. 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 300,000.

items.q: Round 3,078,169 to the nearest 100,000.
items.e: 3,078,169 is between 3,000,000 and 3,100,000. Look at the ten thousands digit: 7. 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 3,100,000.

items.q: Round 6,939,091 to the nearest 1,000,000.
items.e: 6,939,091 is between 6,000,000 and 7,000,000. Look at the hundred thousands digit: 9. 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 7,000,000.

items.q: Round 4,965,300 to the nearest 100,000.
items.e: 4,965,300 is between 4,900,000 and 5,000,000. Look at the ten thousands digit: 6. 5 or more, so round up. The hundred thousands digit is 9, so rounding up makes 10 hundred thousands. Exchange them for 1 million. Answer: 5,000,000.

items.q: Round 2,397,800 to the nearest 10,000.
items.e: 2,397,800 is between 2,390,000 and 2,400,000. Look at the thousands digit: 7. 5 or more, so round up. The ten thousands digit is 9, so rounding up makes 10 ten thousands. Exchange them for 1 hundred thousand. Answer: 2,400,000.

items.q: Which number rounds to 4,000,000 when you round to the nearest 1,000,000?
items.e: Numbers from 3,500,000 to 4,499,999 round to 4,000,000. 3,612,000 is in that range. 3,450,000 rounds to 3,000,000.

items.q: Which number rounds to 760,000 when you round to the nearest 10,000?
items.e: Numbers from 755,000 to 764,999 round to 760,000. 756,300 is in that range. 765,000 rounds to 770,000.

items.q: What is the smallest whole number that rounds to 300,000 when you round to the nearest 100,000?
items.e: Numbers from 250,000 to 349,999 round to 300,000. 249,999 has 4 ten thousands, so it rounds down to 200,000. The smallest is 250,000.

items.q: Round 6,348,527 to the nearest 1,000, the nearest 100,000 and the nearest 1,000,000. Which list is correct?
items.e: Always round the number you started with. Nearest 1,000: the hundreds digit is 5, so 6,349,000. Nearest 100,000: the ten thousands digit is 4, so 6,300,000. Nearest 1,000,000: the hundred thousands digit is 3, so 6,000,000.

items.q: A diver is 12 m below sea level. A seagull is flying 15 m above sea level, straight above the diver. How far apart are they?
items.e: From 12 m below sea level up to sea level is 12 m. From sea level up to the seagull is 15 m. 12 + 15 = 27 m. (15 − 12 = 3 is the mistake of not crossing 0.)

items.q: The average distance from the Earth to the Moon is 384,400 km. What is this to the nearest 10,000 km?
items.e: 384,400 is between 380,000 and 390,000. Look at the thousands digit: 4. 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 380,000 km.

items.q: Sani has the digit cards 7, 0, 3, 9, 1, 5 and 2. He uses each card once to make the smallest 7-digit number he can. What number does he make?
items.e: Put the smallest digits first, but a 7-digit number cannot start with 0. Start with 1, then 0, then 2, 3, 5, 7, 9: 1,023,579. (0,123,579 is really 123,579, a 6-digit number.)

items.q: A football club’s total attendance for the season was two million, forty thousand and fifty. How is this written in digits?
items.e: 2 million → 2, forty thousand → 040, fifty → 050. Fill every empty place with 0: 2,040,050.

items.q: At midnight the temperature was −8 °C. By 9 am it had risen by 5 degrees. What was the temperature at 9 am?
items.e: Risen means count up. From −8 °C count up 5: −7, −6, −5, −4, −3. It is still below 0: −3 °C.

items.q: At 6 pm the temperature was 3 °C. During the night it fell by 9 degrees. What was the temperature then?
items.e: Fell means count down. Count down 3 to reach 0, then 6 more: −6 °C. (3 − 9 is not 6.)

items.q: The population of a town, rounded to the nearest 10,000, is 250,000. What is the smallest the population could be?
items.e: Numbers from 245,000 to 254,999 round to 250,000. 244,999 would round down to 240,000, so the smallest is 245,000. (254,999 is the greatest.)

items.q: At the 2,021 census, Leeds had a population of 811,953. What is this rounded to the nearest 10,000?
items.e: 811,953 is between 810,000 and 820,000. Look at the thousands digit: 1. 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 810,000 people.

items.q: A freezer is at −18 °C. A fridge is at 4 °C. How many degrees warmer is the fridge?
items.e: Count in two jumps through 0. From −18 °C to 0 °C is 18. From 0 °C to 4 °C is 4. 18 + 4 = 22 degrees. Do not work out 18 − 4.

items.q: A newspaper says “about 60,000 fans” went to a concert. The number was rounded to the nearest 1,000. Which could be the real number of fans?
items.e: Numbers from 59,500 to 60,499 round to 60,000. 59,612 is in that range. 60,512 and 60,500 round up to 61,000, and 59,412 rounds down to 59,000.

items.q: A submarine is at −250 m (250 m below sea level). It rises 180 m. Where is it now?
items.e: Rising means count up. −250 + 180: it is still 70 m below sea level, so −70 m.

items.q: In a shopping centre, the ground floor is level 0 and the car park levels are −1 and −2. Babatunde takes the lift from level 3 down to level −2. How many levels does he go down?
items.e: From level 3 down to 0 is 3 levels. From 0 down to −2 is 2 levels. 3 + 2 = 5 levels.

items.q: A museum had 1,463,000 visitors in a year. Gbenga rounds this to the nearest 100,000 first, then rounds his answer to the nearest 1,000,000 and gets 2,000,000. What is 1,463,000 rounded to the nearest 1,000,000?
items.e: Always round the original number. Look at the hundred thousands digit of 1,463,000: 4. 4 or less, so round down to 1,000,000. Rounding twice (1,463,000 → 1,500,000 → 2,000,000) gives the wrong answer.

items.q: A crowd of 74,310 fans watched a cup final. What is the crowd to the nearest 1,000?
items.e: 74,310 is between 74,000 and 75,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 3. 4 or less, so round down. Answer: 74,000 fans.

items.q: A theme park had 1,995,800 visitors last year. This year it had 10,000 more. How many visitors did it have this year?
items.e: Add 1 to the ten thousands digit: 9 + 1 = 10, so exchange for 1 hundred thousand. Then 9 + 1 = 10 hundred thousands, so exchange for 1 million. 1,995,800 + 10,000 = 2,005,800.

items.q: In a shopping centre, the ground floor is level 0 and the car park levels are −1 and −2. Chinedu takes the lift from level 3 down to level −2. How many levels does he go down?
items.e: From level 3 down to 0 is 3 levels. From 0 down to −2 is 2 levels. 3 + 2 = 5 levels.

items.q: Bayo has the digit cards 7, 0, 3, 9, 1, 5 and 2. He uses each card once to make the smallest 7-digit number he can. What number does he make?
items.e: Put the smallest digits first, but a 7-digit number cannot start with 0. Start with 1, then 0, then 2, 3, 5, 7, 9: 1,023,579. (0,123,579 is really 123,579, a 6-digit number.)

items.q: A museum had 1,463,000 visitors in a year. Ikenna rounds this to the nearest 100,000 first, then rounds his answer to the nearest 1,000,000 and gets 2,000,000. What is 1,463,000 rounded to the nearest 1,000,000?
items.e: Always round the original number. Look at the hundred thousands digit of 1,463,000: 4. 4 or less, so round down to 1,000,000. Rounding twice (1,463,000 → 1,500,000 → 2,000,000) gives the wrong answer.

items.q: A museum had 1,463,000 visitors in a year. Nkechi rounds this to the nearest 100,000 first, then rounds her answer to the nearest 1,000,000 and gets 2,000,000. What is 1,463,000 rounded to the nearest 1,000,000?
items.e: Always round the original number. Look at the hundred thousands digit of 1,463,000: 4. 4 or less, so round down to 1,000,000. Rounding twice (1,463,000 → 1,500,000 → 2,000,000) gives the wrong answer.

items.q: Ifeanyi has the digit cards 7, 0, 3, 9, 1, 5 and 2. He uses each card once to make the smallest 7-digit number he can. What number does he make?
items.e: Put the smallest digits first, but a 7-digit number cannot start with 0. Start with 1, then 0, then 2, 3, 5, 7, 9: 1,023,579. (0,123,579 is really 123,579, a 6-digit number.)

items.q: What is 100,000 less than 898,680?
items.e: Only the hundred thousands digit changes: 798,680.

items.q: What is 1,000 more than 301,343?
items.e: Only the thousands digit changes: 302,343.

items.q: What is 100 more than 260,136?
items.e: Only the hundreds digit changes: 260,236.

items.q: What is 100,000 less than 848,360?
items.e: Only the hundred thousands digit changes: 748,360.

items.q: What is 100 more than 832,543?
items.e: Only the hundreds digit changes: 832,643.

items.q: What is 1,000 more than 894,289?
items.e: Only the thousands digit changes: 895,289.

items.q: What is 10,000 more than 261,016?
items.e: Only the ten thousands digit changes: 271,016.

items.q: What is 10,000 more than 558,633?
items.e: Only the ten thousands digit changes: 568,633.

items.q: What is 100,000 more than 203,534?
items.e: Only the hundred thousands digit changes: 303,534.

items.q: What is 100 more than 274,336?
items.e: Only the hundreds digit changes: 274,436.

items.q: Count on in 50s. What comes next? 1,100, 1,150, 1,200, 1,250, …
items.e: Each number is 50 more than the one before: 1,250 + 50 = 1,300.

items.q: Count on in 500s. What comes next? 26,750, 27,250, 27,750, 28,250, …
items.e: Each number is 500 more than the one before: 28,250 + 500 = 28,750.

items.q: Count on in 7s. What comes next? 119, 126, 133, 140, …
items.e: Each number is 7 more than the one before: 140 + 7 = 147.
Each number is 1,000 more than the one before: 20,000 + 1,000 = 21,000.

items.q: Count on in 25s. What comes next? 775, 800, 825, 850, …
items.e: Each number is 25 more than the one before: 850 + 25 = 875.

items.q: Count on in 25s. What comes next? 475, 500, 525, 550, …
items.e: Each number is 25 more than the one before: 550 + 25 = 575.
Each number is 1,000 more than the one before: 61,000 + 1,000 = 62,000.

items.q: Count on in 25s. What comes next? 600, 625, 650, 675, …
items.e: Each number is 25 more than the one before: 675 + 25 = 700.

items.q: Count on in 5s. What comes next? 5, 10, 15, 20, …
items.e: Each number is 5 more than the one before: 20 + 5 = 25.

items.q: Count on in 5s. What comes next? 45, 50, 55, 60, …
items.e: Each number is 5 more than the one before: 60 + 5 = 65.
